c10d8778-5113-4a62-9cf0-d4be824521bc.name: accounting-connection-check
c10d8778-5113-4a62-9cf0-d4be824521bc.description: How the owner connects Dinero's own server after install, how to limit it to a list of allowed tools, what the connection check looks at, why the sign-in can run out, and what to tell the owner when something is wrong.
c10d8778-5113-4a62-9cf0-d4be824521bc.content:
---
name: accounting-connection-check
description: How the owner connects Dinero's own server after install, and the check the Bookkeeper runs at the start of every job and every week. Load at the start of every receipt job and in the weekly connection check. Says what the owner must do and what to tell them when something is wrong.
---

# Accounting connection check

## What the owner does after install

This is an early version. Dinero's own server needs a sign-in that the flow cannot keep alive, so the flow works only while a person supplies a fresh token.

1. In Settings, under Integrations, add Dinero's own server as a custom tool: its address is mcp.dinero.dk, the root with no path. Try it first on a clean test company.
2. Sign in to Dinero through Visma with a user that can see only the one company the flow should work in. The token comes out of that sign-in. It is not on a page in Dinero, so this step needs someone technical. Put the token in the tool as the Authorization header. Never paste the token in the chat.
3. Limit the tool to reading and saving drafts, so the tools that book, change, delete, pay or send are not offered. Dinero's server offers all of them, and the Custom tools form has no field for the allowed list yet, so someone technical sets it through the API: find the tool's id with GET /api/custom-mcp-servers, then send PUT /api/custom-mcp-servers/{id} with the same name and server as before (keep the header values as they are shown) and add allowed_tools to the server, with exactly these 16 names:
   CreatePurchaseVoucher, list_organizations, list_accounting_years, get_chart_of_accounts, list_purchase_accounts, list_vat_types, list_contacts, get_contact, GetContactByName, list_vouchers, get_purchase_voucher, list_files, list_voucher_file_cards, get_purchase_drafts_for_file, SearchBankTransactions, upload_file.
   The names are exact, capitals as shown. Every other tool is left out of the tool list and refused, whatever access the Bookkeeper has. CreatePurchaseVoucher saves a draft and cannot book. upload_file only attaches the receipt. Never add CreateFinanceVoucher (it books in the same call when its book option is on), BookVoucher, book_finance_voucher, every tool whose name starts with delete_, send_trade_offer, add_invoice_payment, add_purchase_payment and attach_file_to_voucher_card. If Dinero renames a tool, the call fails and the check below says so.
4. Give the Bookkeeper read and write access to the tool. At read only it can look but not save a draft.

The sign-in token runs out after about an hour and the flow cannot renew it. When it runs out, Dinero answers with a sign-in error, and a person has to get a fresh token and replace it. Until then the flow cannot reach Dinero.

## The check, at the start of every job

1. Look at the Dinero tools you have. If there are none, the owner has not finished steps 1 to 4: say so and stop.
2. Make one read call that needs no input, such as listing the organisations or the vouchers. If it returns data, the connection works.
3. Check that you have the tool that creates a purchase voucher as a draft. If you do not, say so and stop.
4. Check that you have no tool that books, posts, changes, deletes, pays or sends anything to a customer, and that every Dinero tool you have is on the list in step 3 of the install steps. If you have one that is not, say so and stop. Do not call it, even if the owner asks. The tool get_vat_report is not a Dinero tool and does not count here: it is not on the list, it is not a reason to stop, and its absence does not mean the connection is broken.
5. Say which company the data belongs to if the tools show a name, so the owner can confirm it is the right one.

## What to say when it fails

Say it in one short plain line each and tell the owner the one thing to do:
- No Dinero tools: add Dinero's server under Integrations and give the Bookkeeper access.
- A sign-in or 401 error: the Dinero token has run out, which happens about every hour. Get a fresh token and replace it. Say that this early version needs a person to reconnect each time.
- No draft tool: the Bookkeeper has read access only, or CreatePurchaseVoucher is not on the allowed list. Set it to read and write and check the list.
- A tool that books, changes or deletes is offered, or a Dinero tool that is not on the allowed list: the tool is not limited to drafts. Set the allowed list from step 3 of the install steps before anything is saved.
- Wrong company: the sign-in sees another company. Sign in with a user that sees the right one.
- Too many requests: wait a minute and try again.

Never try to work around a failed check by guessing, by asking for the token in chat, or by calling a different tool.

## The weekly check

Run the same check without any receipt. If it works, say nothing. If it fails, post one short comment on the flow with the line above that fits. A sign-in that has run out is expected between visits, so say it once and do not repeat it.

3f50612b-123a-465b-9a46-70b3c58135c4.name: bookkeeping-draft-method
3f50612b-123a-465b-9a46-70b3c58135c4.description: How the Bookkeeper reads a receipt, saves a draft voucher, runs the rule check and lists what looks wrong for the owner. Draft only.
3f50612b-123a-465b-9a46-70b3c58135c4.content:
---
name: bookkeeping-draft-method
description: How the Bookkeeper reads a receipt, drafts a voucher and lists what looks wrong. Load when the owner uploads a receipt. Draft only, nothing is ever booked.
---

# Bookkeeping draft method

## Hard rules

- Draft only. Nothing is booked, filed or signed. A person approves every draft in the accounting system.
- Never guess an amount. If a receipt is unreadable or an amount is unclear, put it on the list and ask a person.
- Plain words in anything an owner reads. Every item on the list says why in one plain line.

## Step 1: read the receipt

Read the date, payee, receipt number, total including VAT, the VAT amount and the currency. Say what you could not read. A receipt you cannot read at all goes on the list with no draft.

## Step 2: draft the voucher

Fill the voucher fields from the receipt: date, text, amount including VAT, VAT amount, amount excluding VAT, a suggested account in plain words (for example software or fuel) and the receipt file attached. Save it as a draft voucher in Dinero with the draft tool and attach the receipt file to it. Never book it.

Danish VAT basics, for a Danish company:
- The standard rate is 25 percent. VAT is 20 percent of the amount including VAT (divide by 1.25 for the amount excluding VAT).
- No VAT or a different treatment: wages, bank fees, insurance, most financial items, some EU and non-EU purchases (reverse charge). Do not guess these. Save the draft with a note, or put it on the list.
- Restaurant and entertainment: only a part is deductible. Put it on the list.
- The suggested account is a suggestion in plain words, never an account number the owner could mistake for a decision.

## Step 3: run the rule check

Load the skill accounting-rule-check and test every saved draft against its rules. Write the clear or flagged result for each entry in the table that skill describes. The five kinds of mistake below are still looked for, and each one you find also goes on the list. Never save a second draft, or change the first, to make an entry pass.

## Step 4: look for the five kinds of mistake

Check each receipt, and the vouchers already in Dinero when you can read them, for:
1. Missing receipt: a bank line or voucher with no receipt.
2. VAT that does not add up: VAT on the receipt is not 20 percent of the amount including VAT, or it is missing where it should be there.
3. Double payment: the same payee and amount twice within 14 days, or the same receipt number twice.
4. Private cost: a payee or text that looks private, such as groceries, clothes, streaming at home or family travel, paid from the business account.
5. Odd amount: far outside what this payee usually charges, a round amount with no receipt, or a payee not seen before for a large sum.

## Step 5: the list for the owner

One list for the whole session. Flagged entries come first, biggest amount at stake first, each with its rule ids, then the other items and notes. The list also holds the result table from the rule check. Each item: the receipt or voucher, the kind of mistake, one plain sentence on why, and what it could cost the owner if left (in kroner if known, otherwise say not known). Say looks like, never state a doubt as a fact. Save the list as a file in the flow and link it in the chat.

## Step 6: tell the owner

In the chat: how many receipts came in, how many are saved as drafts, how many are clear and how many are flagged by the rule check, how many are on the list and at most five questions only the owner can answer, one sentence each. Do not promise anything beyond the drafts.

## Before you finish

Count receipts in, drafts saved, rows clear plus rows flagged, and items on the list, and check they add up. Say what you could not read or decide.

6c299902-7577-40a4-9bee-ddc6aedd79a2.name: accounting-rule-check
6c299902-7577-40a4-9bee-ddc6aedd79a2.description: The written rule list every draft voucher is tested against before the owner sees it, and the clear or flagged result for every entry. Draft only.
6c299902-7577-40a4-9bee-ddc6aedd79a2.content:
---
name: accounting-rule-check
description: The written rule list every draft voucher is tested against before the owner sees it, and the clear or flagged result written for every entry. Load after each draft is saved, at the start of the list for the owner. Draft only, nothing is ever booked.
---

# Accounting rule check

Every draft voucher is tested against the rules below before the owner sees it. An entry that breaks no flag rule is clear. An entry that breaks one is flagged, with the rule id and one plain line why. The check only reads the draft. It never changes a voucher and never books one. A person approves every draft in Dinero: clear does not mean approved.

The rules come from the Danish VAT act (momsloven), the bookkeeping act (bogføringsloven) and Skat's own guidance, and each rule names its source. Do not add rules from memory, and do not change a rate or a limit.

## Company facts, asked once

Some rules need three facts about the company. Read the open accounting year from Dinero. Ask the owner the other two once, at the start of the first job in a chat, in one short message: does the firm get full VAT deduction (not a holding company, no VAT-exempt activity), and has any VAT period already been filed, and up to which date. Keep the answers at the top of the list file. If the owner has not answered, rules R18 and R30 flag every entry and the list says why.

## How to run it

1. After each draft is saved, test it against every rule, in order, using only what you hold: date, payee, receipt number, total including VAT, VAT amount, currency, VAT code, suggested account, the receipt file and what you read on it, the company facts above, and the vouchers already in Dinero.
2. A rule whose input is missing or unreadable cannot pass. It flags, and the line says which input is missing.
3. A rule marked unsourced flags whenever the situation it describes is present. Never pass it on your own judgement. A situation that is not present is not a flag: an entry is not flagged by a rule just because the rule is unsourced.
4. Use the owner line of the rule, with the amounts filled in. Say looks like, never state a doubt as a fact.
5. Never change an amount, an account or a VAT code to make an entry pass. A failed rule means the entry is flagged. That is the point.
6. When R5 fires because no receipt is attached, write R5 and say the rules that need the receipt (R2, R3, R7 to R20) were not tested. Do not list them one by one.
7. An entry you read with low confidence (a blurry photo, a handwritten receipt, an amount you had to guess at) is flagged with the rule R3 and the line says what was unclear.

## The result, one row per entry

Write one table in the list file, one row per entry, with these columns in this order so that another step can read it:

| entry | result | rules | why |

- entry: the voucher or receipt as the owner knows it (date, payee, amount).
- result: exactly clear or flagged.
- rules: the ids of every flag rule the entry broke, for example R2 and R7. Empty only when the result is clear.
- why: one plain line for each rule, using its owner line.

An entry is also flagged when it is on the list of what looks wrong for any of the five kinds of mistake in the draft method (missing receipt, VAT that does not add up, double payment, private cost, odd amount). Put the kind in rules, in words, and say why in the same plain line. An entry on that list is never clear.

Any step that reads this table treats every entry that is not exactly clear as flagged. A note rule is written in why but does not make an entry flagged.

## The list for the owner

Flagged entries come first, biggest amount at stake first, each with its rule ids and lines. Then the notes. Count the rows: entries in, rows clear, rows flagged, and check they add up.

## The rules

Each rule has an id, a test, a source, the line the owner reads, a severity and a status. Severity flag stops an entry being clear. Severity note is shown but does not. Status unsourced means no source was opened for the exact test: when the situation the rule describes is present, the rule flags and the owner decides in Dinero. It is never passed on your own judgement.

R1 | flag | unsourced | Test: the debit lines and the credit lines of the draft add up to the same amount in kroner, VAT lines included. It flags when the two sides differ, or when the draft has no lines to compare. | Source: bogføringsloven § 7 stk. 1 and § 8. | Owner line: This entry looks like it does not balance, the two sides differ by [amount] kr.
R2 | flag | sourced | Test: the VAT on the entry equals the rate of its VAT code times the base. For 25 percent on a total including VAT, VAT is 20 percent of the total, within 0.01 kr (the tolerance is a setting of this flow, not a rule from a source). | Source: momsloven § 33; Skat A.B.3.3.1.6. | Owner line: The VAT on this entry looks wrong, 25 percent VAT is 20 percent of the total, so on [total] kr it should be about [x] kr, not [y] kr.
R3 | flag | sourced | Test: date, total, VAT, currency and payee on the entry equal the same fields read from the attached receipt. | Source: bogføringsloven § 9 stk. 2. | Owner line: The entry looks different from the receipt: [field] says [entry value] here and [receipt value] on the receipt.
R4 | flag | sourced | Test: if the currency is not DKK, a rate or a kroner amount for the day of the payment is on the entry. | Source: bogføringsloven § 10 stk. 2. | Owner line: This looks like a [currency] payment with no exchange rate, so the kroner amount cannot be checked.
R5 | flag | sourced | Test: a receipt file is attached and readable (not empty, not another document). | Source: bogføringsloven § 9 stk. 1 and § 15 stk. 1 nr. 1; momsloven § 52 c stk. 1 nr. 2; Skat guidance on VAT deduction. | Owner line: There looks to be no receipt on this entry, and VAT cannot be claimed without one.
R6 | note | sourced | Test: the receipt number or invoice number is in the entry text. | Source: bogføringsloven § 9 stk. 1 and stk. 2. | Owner line: The receipt number looks missing from this entry, so it is harder to trace later.
R7 | flag | sourced | Test: if VAT is claimed, the receipt shows seller name, seller CVR or VAT number, date, number and the VAT amount. Above 3,000 kr it also shows the buyer's name and address. | Source: Skat A.B.3.3.1.4 and A.B.3.3.1.6. | Owner line: This receipt looks too thin to claim VAT on: [missing item] is not on it.
R8 | flag | sourced | Test: a Danish seller with a CVR number and a VAT line means the code is domestic input VAT at 25 percent, and R2 holds. | Source: momsloven § 33 and § 37 stk. 1 and stk. 2 nr. 1. | Owner line: This looks like an ordinary Danish purchase with 25 percent VAT, but the entry uses [code].
R9 | flag | sourced | Test: a receipt with no VAT amount, or from a VAT-exempt supplier (insurance, bank and finance fees, rent of property, health, education), means the code is no VAT and no input VAT is claimed. | Source: momsloven § 13 stk. 1 nr. 1, 3, 8, 10 and 11; § 37 stk. 2 nr. 1; § 52 a stk. 6. | Owner line: This looks like a purchase without VAT, but the entry claims [x] kr input VAT.
R10 | flag | sourced | Test: an EU seller outside Denmark, a service, and no VAT on the receipt means the code is reverse charge for services, with VAT at 25 percent of the receipt amount, reported as EU services. | Source: Skat page on VAT when buying from EU; momsloven § 16 stk. 1 and § 46 stk. 1 nr. 3; Skat D.A.13.2.2.3. | Owner line: This looks like a service from an EU company, so the Danish VAT must be calculated by us, and the entry does not.
R11 | flag | sourced | Test: an EU seller outside Denmark, goods, and no VAT on the receipt means the code is reverse charge for EU goods, with VAT at 25 percent of the receipt amount, reported as EU goods. | Source: Skat page on VAT when buying from EU; momsloven § 46 stk. 4; Skat A.B.3.3.3.2.4. | Owner line: This looks like goods bought from an EU company, so the Danish VAT is ours to calculate, and the entry does not.
R12 | flag | sourced | Test: a seller in another EU country shows VAT (Danish or foreign) on a business purchase. | Source: Skat page on VAT when buying from EU (ask the seller for a new invoice). | Owner line: This looks like an EU supplier that added VAT, and Skat says to ask them for a new invoice without it.
R13 | flag | sourced | Test: a seller outside the EU, a service with no special place-of-supply rule, means reverse charge for services with the same figures as R10. | Source: momsloven § 46 stk. 1 nr. 3; Skat D.A.13.2.2.3; Skat page on VAT when buying from outside the EU. | Owner line: This looks like a service from a company outside the EU, so the Danish VAT must be calculated by us, and the entry does not.
R14 | flag | unsourced | Test: a seller abroad and the item is a hotel, event ticket, restaurant or catering, short-term car rental, transport or work on property. The default reverse charge of R10 and R13 is not applied blindly. | Source: momsloven §§ 18, 19 and 21 read in part. | Owner line: This looks like a service abroad that has its own VAT rule, so the VAT code here looks like a guess.
R15 | flag | sourced | Test: goods from outside the EU: the VAT on the entry equals the import VAT on the customs or carrier bill, not the seller's invoice. | Source: momsloven § 46 stk. 6. | Owner line: This looks like an import from outside the EU, and the VAT should follow the customs bill, which looks different here.
R16 | flag | sourced | Test: a reverse charge entry (R10, R11, R13) has an output VAT line and an input VAT line, both 25 percent of the base. The input line is only there if the company has full deduction. | Source: momsloven § 56 stk. 2 and 3 and § 37 stk. 2 nr. 2. | Owner line: This reverse charge entry looks one-sided, VAT is [owed only or deducted only], so the VAT return would be off by [x] kr.
R17 | flag | sourced | Test: the entry date is inside the company's open accounting year. | Source: bogføringsloven § 9 stk. 1 and § 7 stk. 1. | Owner line: This date looks outside the open accounting year, so it cannot be booked as it stands.
R18 | flag | sourced | Test: the entry date is not inside a VAT period that is already filed. | Source: momsloven § 56 stk. 1 and 3 and § 57 stk. 4; Skat page on correcting a VAT return. | Owner line: This looks like it belongs to a VAT period already sent to Skat, so it needs a correction, not a normal booking.
R19 | flag | sourced | Test: the receipt date is more than 3 years before the filing deadline of its VAT period. | Source: Skat page on correcting a VAT return (3 years). | Owner line: This receipt looks older than the 3 years Skat allows for VAT, so the VAT on it is probably lost.
R20 | flag | sourced | Test: the same payee and the same receipt number already exist in another entry, draft or booked. | Source: bogføringsloven § 7 stk. 1; Skat A.B.3.3.1.4. | Owner line: This looks like a receipt we already have, it matches entry [id].
R21 | flag | unsourced | Test: the same payee, total and currency within 14 days of another entry, with a different or missing receipt number. The 14 days are a setting of this flow, the same as the double payment check in the draft method, not a rule from a source. | Source: bogføringsloven § 7 stk. 1 supports it, no source gives a window. | Owner line: This looks like a possible double payment, same amount to the same payee as entry [id].
R22 | flag | sourced | Test: a credit note or negative amount refers to the original invoice, and its VAT code and rate equal the original entry's with the signs reversed. | Source: momsloven § 52 a stk. 5; Skat A.B.3.3.1.4. | Owner line: This credit note looks like it does not undo the original, the VAT differs by [x] kr.
R23 | flag | sourced | Test: a restaurant, café or catering: input VAT is at most 25 percent of the VAT on the receipt, and the cost is strictly business. | Source: momsloven § 42 stk. 1 nr. 5 and stk. 2; Skat page on VAT on food and hotels. | Owner line: This looks like a restaurant bill, and only 25 percent of the VAT can be deducted, so [x] kr is too much.
R24 | flag | sourced | Test: a hotel invoice is split into the stay and the food. The stay carries full VAT, breakfast and restaurant carry 25 percent of their VAT. An unsplit invoice flags. | Source: Skat page on VAT on food and hotels. | Owner line: This looks like a hotel bill, and the stay and the food must be split before the VAT can be set.
R25 | flag | sourced | Test: entertainment (tickets, events, activities for staff or clients): input VAT on the entry is zero. | Source: momsloven § 42 stk. 1 nr. 5; Skat page on VAT on food and hotels. | Owner line: This looks like entertainment, and VAT on that cannot be deducted, so the [x] kr should not be claimed.
R26 | flag | sourced | Test: gifts (gift items, flowers, wine, gift cards, staff presents): input VAT on the entry is zero. | Source: momsloven § 42 stk. 1 nr. 5 (the act text only). | Owner line: This looks like a gift, and VAT on gifts cannot be deducted, so the [x] kr should not be claimed.
R27 | flag | sourced | Test: a passenger car (white plates): purchase, fuel, repairs, insurance and parking carry no input VAT. The exceptions (Øresund bridge toll, a lease over 6 months with 10 percent business driving) need the owner's facts. | Source: momsloven § 42 stk. 1 nr. 6, stk. 4 and stk. 7; Skat page on VAT on car costs. | Owner line: This looks like a cost for a passenger car, and VAT on those cannot be deducted, so [x] kr should not be claimed.
R28 | flag | sourced | Test: the receipt or entry text names food, drink, a home or a living cost for the owner or staff (groceries, staff meals, rent of a home, benefits in kind): input VAT is zero. A cost with no such word on it is not flagged by this rule. | Source: momsloven § 42 stk. 1 nr. 1 to 3. | Owner line: This looks like a food or living cost for people, not for the business, so the VAT on it cannot be deducted.
R29 | flag | sourced | Test: the payee or account is mixed use (phone, internet, computer, home office, retail shop) and the full VAT is claimed with no business share on the entry. | Source: momsloven § 38 stk. 2; Skat pages on VAT deduction and on fixed costs. | Owner line: This looks like it could be partly private, and only the business share of the VAT can be deducted.
R30 | flag | sourced | Test: the company is not fully VAT-registered with full deduction (holding company, VAT-exempt activity, mixed activity) and the entry claims input VAT. | Source: momsloven § 37 stk. 1 and § 38 stk. 1. | Owner line: This company looks like it may not have full VAT deduction, so the [x] kr input VAT needs a check.
R31 | flag | unsourced | Test: a representation cost, a gift or a possibly private cost: the income tax limit for the company is applied or noted. | Source: none opened, this is income tax, not VAT. | Owner line: This looks like a cost with its own income tax limit, so part of it may not count as a business cost for tax.
R32 | flag | unsourced | Test: the total is more than 3 times the usual amount for the same payee (the middle of the payee's other entries), or the payee has no earlier entry and the total is 2,000 kr or more without a receipt. The 3 times and the 2,000 kr are settings of this flow, not rules from a source. | Source: none opened, this is a plausibility check. | Owner line: This amount looks far out of line, [total] kr against about [usual] kr that this payee usually charges.

bebb1314-b2d0-43d3-8ba1-a5bcbf5db7ea.name: vat-return-check
bebb1314-b2d0-43d3-8ba1-a5bcbf5db7ea.description: How the Bookkeeper checks the figures before a VAT return is due and writes the draft check note. Load in the weekly VAT return check and whenever the owner asks for it. Never files anything.
bebb1314-b2d0-43d3-8ba1-a5bcbf5db7ea.content:
---
name: vat-return-check
description: How the Bookkeeper checks the figures before a VAT return is due and writes the draft check note. Load in the weekly VAT return check and whenever the owner asks for it. Never files anything.
---

# VAT return check

A draft check of the VAT figures, so the owner can look before filing in Dinero. The flow never files, signs or pays, and nothing it writes claims that a return went out.

## Hard rules

- The figures come from the tool get_vat_report and from nothing else. Do not add up vouchers yourself and do not build a second set of figures. If the tool is not among your tools, say so in the first line of your output: the check needs Dinero connected by sign-in, so the flow can read its own VAT report. Name the owner as the one who can connect it, and stop.
- get_vat_report is not a Dinero tool. It only reads, and it is allowed even though it is not one of the 16 names. The connection check does not count it.
- Every date comes from Skat at run time and is cited with the page address. Nothing is coded into this skill and nothing is taken from memory or from Dinero. Never guess a date. A rate, a limit or a deadline you did not read on the page is not written.
- Say looks like, never state a doubt as a fact. The owner decides in Dinero.
- Both amounts on every finding: with VAT and without VAT. Where the report does not calculate the VAT on a line, say so and show the amount as booked.
- Plain words in the owner's own language, short. Link every object and file you name.

## Step 1: the period and the due date

1. Read the owner's VAT period (monthly, quarterly or half-yearly) from the owner's context page, the one page the flow keeps the owner's facts and the next dates on (find it with list_objects, type knowledge, q context). If there is none, use the answer on the setup child task named Confirm the VAT period.
2. Take the next VAT due date from the same context page if it is there, was written in the last week and carries a Skat page address. Otherwise open the Skat page on VAT deadlines and read the date for the owner's period. Cite the page address you read.
3. Read the start and end of the VAT period that date belongs to from the same page. If you cannot confirm the period or the date, the first line of the note says due date not confirmed and names who can supply it (the owner, or whoever files for them). Do not guess.

## Step 2: decide whether to run

- Due date more than 28 days away: stay silent, write nothing and post nothing.
- Due date within 28 days: run the full check.
- Due date within 20 days: run the short version, which is the first lines, the total and the findings table, with the clean list cut to one line.
- Due date not confirmed: run once for the period, and say so on the first line.
- A note for this period may already exist: look for a knowledge page titled VAT check, then the period start, the word to, and the period end. If it exists and carries the same figures hash as the new report, do nothing. If the hash differs, write a new note with the same title and mark the old one deprecated.

## Step 3: read the figures

1. Call get_vat_report with the period start as from and the period end as to. It returns the report lines per VAT code and a check with the findings, already ranked by kroner at stake, biggest first.
2. Call list_vat_types. If the codes the check treats as purchases from abroad (IEUV, IEUY, IVV, IVY) do not mean that in Dinero's list, say so in one line in the note and treat those findings as unconfirmed.
3. If the report says it is not complete, say how many lines use a VAT code it does not calculate. A gap in the figures is itself a finding.

## Step 4: write the note

Create one knowledge page, at status draft, titled exactly VAT check, the period start, the word to, the period end, so the review screen can find it. Put the figures hash from the report in the last line. Link it to the flow with an in_loop relationship from the flow (find the flow named Accounting with list_loops). In this order:

1. First line: the period, the due date with its Skat page address, or due date not confirmed and who can supply it.
2. One line: a draft for checking, not the VAT return. This check files nothing, the owner files in Dinero.
3. Total kroner at stake first, then how many lines the report does not calculate and so are not in the total.
4. A ranked table, one row per finding: voucher date and text, the amount with VAT, the VAT, the amount without VAT, the rule ids, whether it is confirmed or unconfirmed, and one plain line on what looks off. Foreign suppliers (reverse charge) have no VAT figure here: show the amount as booked and say the Danish VAT is not calculated in the report, so the owner checks it in Dinero against rules R10, R11, R13 and R16 of the accounting-rule-check skill. Odd rates are lines under a VAT code that is not 25 percent or no VAT. Private costs are lines whose text looks like food, a gift, entertainment, a car or a restaurant, with input VAT claimed.
5. What was checked and found clean: the kinds of finding with none, and that the totals come from the same report the review screen shows.
6. One line on correcting a filed return, from the Skat page on correcting a VAT return, read now and cited: a filed return can be corrected, normally within three years, and the owner files the correction.
7. Last line: the figures hash from the report.

## Step 5: tell the owner, only when it matters

Only when the due date is within 28 days, post one short comment on the flow: the due date, the number of findings, the total kroner at stake and the link to the note. Otherwise say nothing. Never claim that a return went out.
